newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia '96/97 cotton still at record - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia '96/97 cotton still at record - ABARE.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) has only marginally shaved its forecast for Australia's 1996/97 (July/June) cotton crop, despite recent heavy rain.
The crop is now forecast to emerge at a record 552,000 tonnes, up from 429,000 tonnes in 1995/96.

"Heavy rains in the Namoi and Darling Downs regions (in the states of New South Wales and Queendsland) in early 1997 resulted in only minor damage to the cotton crop," ABARE said in its Australian Commodities forecasts, issued on Tuesday.
"Moreover, the rains in other cotton growing areas (of the two states) were generally beneficial," ABARE said.
The 1997/98 crop is forecast to decline slightly to 547,000 tonnes of lint, it said.
This forecast is down from the 557,000 tonnes forecast for 1997/98 at ABARE's Outlook conference in February.
The forecast for 1996/97 production at the Outlook conference was for 571,000 tonnes of lint, steady with ABARE's forecast last December.
